# FOLO
> FOLO Only Looks Once: a from-scratch Rust vision framework. It has its own tensors, autograd, CPU kernels and
> wgpu/WGSL GPU kernels, a YOLO-style detector (folo-n/s/m/l/x), and training, evaluation and export. It ships one
> `folo` CLI (every command supports `--json`, with stable exit codes), an HTTP + SSE API (`folo serve`), an MCP
> server for agents (`folo mcp`), the FOLO Studio web app, the FOLO Desktop native app, and in-browser inference
> (wasm + WebGPU). Status: v0.1, early. COCO-pretrained weights are published GitHub releases (`folo weights pull
> folo-n-coco-v2`, folo-n, val2017 AP 0.317; `folo weights pull folo-s-coco`, folo-s, AP 0.416; the repository is
> private for now, so that needs access to it through `gh`); the 0.1.0 binary release is a draft (build from source).

Fastest path for an agent:
- **MCP:** `folo mcp --data-dir DIR` (stdio). It has 22 tools: folo_info, list_datasets, get_dataset,
  list_dataset_issues, list_dataset_images, register_dataset, create_synthetic_dataset, list_models, train,
  run_status, list_runs, stop_run, reorder_run, val, predict, predict_batch, export, compare_runs,
  cloud_connections, cloud_offers, cloud_instances and cloud_terminate.
- **CLI:** `folo <command> --json`. stdout is then JSON Lines only. Errors end with
  `{"error":{"code","message","hint"}}`. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 runtime, 2 usage, 3 not found, 4 not implemented.
- **Discovery:** `folo describe --json` prints every command, argument and default, plus every MCP tool's input and
  output schemas.
- **From a checkout:** `cargo folo ...` (an alias for `cargo run --release -p folo-cli -- ...`).

## Start here
- [README](README.md): the pitch, benchmark headline vs Ultralytics yolo26n, 60-second quickstart, Studio and
  Desktop, agent setup (Claude Code / Codex / .mcp.json), architecture at a glance, project status
- [Quickstart](docs/QUICKSTART.md): the longer walkthrough. It covers building, synthetic data, training on your
  own YOLO or COCO folder, dataset checks, fine-tuning from a .folo file, resume, val, predict, export, Studio,
  in-browser inference and troubleshooting
- [Agent cookbook](docs/AGENT_COOKBOOK.md): recipes in two forms, MCP tool calls and `folo ... --json`. They cover
  training on a folder, comparing runs, finding label problems, export and inference, scripting with --json, and
  sharing runs with Studio
- [MCP server](docs/MCP.md): the `folo mcp` contract. Flags are `[--data-dir D] [--device auto|cpu|gpu:N] [--mock]
  [--read-only] [--confine] [--server URL]`; it speaks MCP 2026-07-28 and 2025-11-25. It documents the tools with
  their JSON Schemas, the `folo://` resources (dataset images, subscribable runs and metrics, sample grids, docs),
  the prompts train_on_folder and diagnose_run, and the errors: `isError` results whose text is
  `{code, message, hint}`
- [CLI](docs/CLI.md): every `folo` command (serve, describe, doctor, train, val, predict, export, dataset
  synth|stats|check|convert, weights, cloud, mcp), its flags and its --json records, plus the error and exit-code conventions

## Reference
- [HTTP API](docs/API.md): the HTTP + SSE contract of `folo serve`, used by Studio, Desktop and `folo mcp --server`.
  It covers datasets, models (weights download), runs (live events), predict, val, export, agent labeling
  (`/api/label`), vision benchmarks (`/api/bench`), uploads, cloud compute (`/api/cloud`), and real vs mock mode
- [Agent labeling](docs/LABELING.md): unlabeled images to a dataset. `folo serve` drives Claude Code or Codex
  (one model request per batch of images, no tools), a person reviews the boxes in Studio, and the result is a
  registered YOLO dataset. It has the workflow, the HTTP calls, what a run costs in tokens and measured accuracy
- [Vision benchmarks](docs/BENCH.md): grade any vision model on your own images. A benchmark is a frozen set of
  labeled images plus a plan of stress conditions (twelve, at severities 1 to 5); an entry is a FOLO model, a
  coding agent or externally made predictions, scored 0 to 100 on five axes (accuracy, robustness, self-labeling,
  calibration, localization), each defined exactly; a self-improvement loop has a model label a pool, trains a
  student on those labels alone and grades it. HTTP API under `/api/bench` (feature `vision_bench`); the engine is
  `crates/folo-bench`. Not the speed benchmark (`folo bench`, docs/BENCHMARKS.md)
- [Cloud compute](docs/CLOUD.md): training runs on a rented GPU (RunPod) or on another FOLO server
  (`TrainConfig.compute`, `folo cloud`, MCP `cloud_*`). It has the lifecycle of a cloud run, how instances are
  never left behind, the providers, and `folo serve --token`
- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the crates (folo-core, folo-gpu, folo-nn, folo-data, folo-vision,
  folo-api, folo-client, folo-cloud, folo-server, folo-mcp, folo-cli, folo-wasm) and how they fit together, with
  the backend contract
- [Detector spec](docs/MODEL.md): the normative spec of folo-n/s/m/l/x. It covers the blocks, the head, the loss,
  the task-aligned assigner, the training recipe and the inference path
- [Data](docs/DATA.md): YOLO and COCO detection rules, label parsing, robustness, augmentation, the data loader,
  dataset checks and conversion
- [Metrics](docs/METRICS.md): how mAP, precision, recall and the confusion matrix are computed (pycocotools parity)
- [NN](docs/NN.md): modules, init, optimizers (SGD, AdamW), LR schedules, EMA, and `.folo` IO
- [File format](docs/FORMAT.md): `.folo` weights and checkpoints (safetensors-compatible) and its metadata
- [GPU](docs/GPU.md): the wgpu backend, buffer pool and WGSL kernels, adapter selection (`FOLO_GPU_ADAPTER`,
  `FOLO_GPU_BACKEND`) and testing
- [In the browser](docs/WASM.md): folo-wasm. It covers the build (`scripts/build-wasm.sh`), the JS API
  (`FoloDetector.load` / `detect`, the /api/predict result shape), WebGPU vs wasm-CPU performance and the browser
  test
- [Benchmarks](docs/BENCHMARKS.md): folo-n/s vs Ultralytics yolo26n/s/m on an RTX 4080 SUPER (GPU forward, end to
  end, CPU, training step, memory), with the method, raw numbers and next optimisations. Scripts and raw JSON are
  in `bench/baselines/`; fine-tuning accuracy on small datasets (folo-n vs yolo26n and folo-s vs yolo26s, one pycocotools scorer) in
  `bench/finetune/`

## Examples
- [Shapes](examples/shapes/README.md): the convergence gate (folo-n on synthetic shapes at 320 px). It has the
  commands and per-epoch results on CPU (72 min) and GPU (169 s)
- [COCO](examples/coco/README.md): folo-n and folo-s pretrained from scratch on COCO 2017 at 640 px (val2017 AP 0.317
  and 0.416), with pycocotools parity and `folo weights`

## Apps
- [FOLO Studio](web/README.md): the web app (Svelte 5 + TypeScript + Vite). It covers the dev server, checks,
  tests, screenshots (`npm run shoot`) and data sources
- [FOLO Desktop](apps/desktop/README.md): the native GPUI app. It covers running it, connecting to `folo serve`,
  `--mock`, `--scenario`, layout and screenshots
- [Design system](design/README.md): the shared design tokens (`design/tokens.json`) both apps generate their
  themes from
- UI hill-climb docs, for UI work only:
  - Studio: [direction](web/DESIGN_DIRECTION.md), [rubric](web/REVIEW_RUBRIC.md), [log](web/HILLCLIMB.md)
  - Desktop: [direction](apps/desktop/DIRECTION.md), [rubric](apps/desktop/REVIEW_RUBRIC.md),
    [log](apps/desktop/HILLCLIMB.md), [review brief](apps/desktop/tools/review-brief.md)

## Project
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): the entry point for Claude Code; it points at AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- [Agent rules](AGENTS.md): the ground rules for contributors (stable Rust, no ML frameworks, tests, docs), build
  hygiene and the layout
- [Process](docs/PROCESS.md): implement → PR → review → fix → merge, and the reviewer setup
- [Roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md): milestones, with what is merged, in progress and next
- [Releasing](docs/RELEASE.md): versioning, the tag → draft release workflow, the install scripts
  (`scripts/install.sh`, `scripts/install.ps1`) and the embedded Studio
- [CI](docs/CI.md): the CI jobs and the self-hosted runners
- [Docs site](site/README.md): the static site generated from these docs (`cd site && npm run build`), with search,
  link checking, and this file plus llms-full.txt (every page's Markdown in one file)
- [boat.dev](docs/BOAT.md): CPU-only cloud sandboxes for offloading Linux builds and CPU-heavy work
- [Dogfood report 1](docs/DOGFOOD-1.md): a fresh agent's friction report from driving FOLO via the CLI and MCP
- [Dogfood report 2](docs/DOGFOOD-2.md): the README quickstart, Studio (Playwright), MCP on real data and Desktop,
  plus which DOGFOOD-1 fixes held
- [Dogfood report 3](docs/DOGFOOD-3.md): the docs site, pretrained weights, AMP, the NMS-free head, ONNX and the
  queue and estimates on real data (CLI, MCP, Studio, Desktop), plus which DOGFOOD-2 fixes held
